t: Aspasia of Miletus | Biography | Research Starters | EBSCO Research
s: Aspasia of Miletus, a prominent figure in ancient Athens, was born in the wealthy trading city of Miletus around 470 BCE. She rose to public attention as the intellectual companion and mistress of the statesman Pericles. Classified as a hetaera, a term referring to educated and often foreign women who engaged socially and intimately with influential men, Aspasia faced substantial criticism and accusations regarding her influence on Pericles' political decisions, particularly during the Peloponnesian War.
